## Summary

For 22 years the pound was pegged at 1,507.5 to the dollar. The peg was held up by deposits that banks lent to the central bank, which used them to fund the state, under a system its critics compare to a Ponzi scheme. In 2019 the dollars stopped coming. Banks froze withdrawals, the state defaulted (March 2020), and the parallel rate went from 1,500 to about **140,000** in March 2023. Steve Hanke counted it as **hyperinflation no. 62, at 52.6 % a month (implied) in July 2020**. Official monthly inflation never reached 50 %, but annual inflation reached **221 % in 2023**.

## Causes

- **"Financial engineering"** by the Banque du Liban from 2016 onwards: it swapped pound debt for
  Eurobonds and paid banks high returns for dollars. The IMF estimates the banks gained $5 billion
  and the central bank lost $13 billion in reserves (Wikipedia).
- **Twin deficits** (fiscal and current account) financed by deposit inflows that stopped in 2019.
- **Political paralysis**, then the **Beirut port explosion of 4 August 2020**.

## Timeline

- **1997** — the peg at 1,507.5.
- **Aug – Oct 2019** — a dollar shortage, the October protests, and informal capital controls by
  the banks.
- **Mar 2020** — default.
- **Jul 2020** — Hanke: 52.6 % a month (implied), hyperinflation no. 62.
- **4 Aug 2020** — the port explosion.
- **Jun 2021** — the World Bank warns that this could be one of the three most severe crises since
  the mid-19th century.
- **Feb 2023** — the official rate is moved to 15,000.
- **Mar 2023** — the parallel peak, about 140,000.
- **Since mid-2023** — about 89,500, stable; the economy runs largely in dollars.

## Where it stands

The rate has been stable since mid-2023 at about 89,500 per dollar, so the site closes the period at 2023.

## Lessons

- A peg is only as strong as the money behind it. Here, "behind it" meant depositors' savings,
  which had been lent to the state.
- It is the bank-run version of hyperinflation. The money did not come from a printing press
  first: it disappeared inside the banking system.
